transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 15:30 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Reed (Redwood SE), Elena Morales (Nova CTO), Marcus Lin (Head of ML), Priya Singh (Cloud Ops)

Summary (auto): Renewal + expansion checkin, customer wants EU + APAC capacity, negotiating 6-month extension, run bench for latency/cost.

00:00 Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick check, is 15:30 still good?
00:06 Elena: Yeah that's perfect, thanks Samira.
00:09 Samira: Cool, so agenda — quick renewal sketch, regions and capacity ask, pricing options, and then Jonah will run through the tech bits then we can wrap with next steps.
00:22 Marcus: Sounds good. We have the deck you sent, that was helpful.
00:26 Samira: Great. So as we discussed over email, Nova's current committed dedicated pool is 8 A100-ish nodes, and your renewal is up in feb, right?
00:37 Elena: Yeah Feb 15. We're trying to avoid an outage window so thinking about a 6-month extension to bridge while we expand into EU and APAC.
00:47 Samira: Got it. The two knobs we usually recommend are committed GPU hours (reserved capacity) and region pinning. For EU/APAC we can regionally replicate dedicated pools or use routing to hosted fallbacks as a stopgap.
01:02 Priya: Quick Q — if we replicate to EU, what about data residency and logs? We need logs kept within region for a subset of requests.
01:12 Jonah: Right, so Redwood Private supports region-specific log retention and KMS integration; for hosted/dedicated we can set your retention policy per-route and S3 bucket regioning, but I'll follow up with the specific SOC2 scope items.
01:25 Marcus: And latency — we've got a hard SLO of sub 200ms p99 for short chat flows, and a lot of your previous numbers are in the 180-260ms range depending on seq len. We need that tightened in EU.
01:38 Jonah: Understood. For EU we can optimize by pinning smaller model variants on EU nodes and using quantized models; also enable prefix KV caching for common prompts — that drops p99 a lot. We'll run a targeted bench with your payload.
01:52 Elena: Pricing concern — doubling regions sounds expensive. Can we get a phased rollout? EU first then APAC?
01:58 Samira: Absolutely. We proposed a phased approach: Phase 1 (Mar) EU dedicated pool sized at 4 nodes, Phase 2 (May) APAC pilot 2 nodes with auto-burst to hosted. For the 6-month extension we can offer a mid-tier discount if you commit to bumped hours.
02:17 Priya: How does burst to hosted work with privacy rules? Some PHI-like payloads must not leave our VPC.
02:24 Jonah: For any traffic flagged as restricted you can mark routes as private-only; Redwood will refuse hosted fallback and instead queue or throttle. Also on Private we can set up an on-prem gateway. Note: transcription might have mis-typed 'queue' as 'cue' in the meeting notes.
02:40 Marcus: (laughs) fair. On the bench: we want to run our 1k conversation sample at p50/p95/p99. Could we do that in EU and compare?
02:50 Jonah: Yes, we'll provision a same-config EU pool and run the tests. A heads up: model selection matters, small-medium variants behave differently with batching. We'll include tokens-per-second and cost per 1M tokens in the spreadsheet.
03:05 Elena: On compliance, SOC2 is required, plus SAML SSO integration. We need to confirm user provisioning and audit logs.
03:13 Samira: We have SOC2 pages and SAML guides. I'll attach SOC2 cert and the SAML SSO setup guide after the call. Jonah will include examples of audit log retention and per-route logging.
03:24 Priya: Can we also get an architecture sketch for how the KV cache interacts with the VPC? Last time the diagram was a bit unclear — it said KV cash in the notes — ha.
03:33 Jonah: Sorry about the autocorrect in the doc. The KV cache sits on the serving layer and respects VPC controls; we'll send a clarified diagram showing subnet placement and KMS flows.
03:45 Marcus: A question on model fallbacks — if EU dedicated is saturated, what's the automated behavior? Do we failover to hosted or to other region?
03:53 Jonah: There are routing policies: prefer local, then prefer dedicated in other region, then hosted with redaction as last resort. You can customize per-route for stricter privacy (no hosted fallback). We'll show policy examples.
04:08 Elena: Good. Pricing — can you walk the discount tiers again?
04:12 Samira: Sure. For the extension: 6 months extension with 20% commit increase gets you 7% off unit price; 40% commit increase gives 12% off; and if you sign a 12-month reserved contract we'll provide an additional enterprise discount. The numbers in the earlier quote were illustrative; I'll send a revised spreadsheet with explicit GPU-hour breakouts.
04:35 Marcus: If we commit more, what's the path to shrink if usage drops? We can't be locked with wasted nodes.
04:40 Samira: We offer a staged commit with an auto-adjust clause: monthly true-up and ability to reallocate unused hours to burst credits. For Dedicated we have a minimum for the contract but we can build a 90-day lookback to avoid big overpay. I'll include the exact language.
04:55 Priya: About KMS keys — can we use our customer-managed keys in GCP KMS?
04:59 Jonah: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations across major clouds; you'll need to set up a key policy and we can provide an IAM template.
05:10 Elena: Ok good. Anything else on security?
05:13 Marcus: Do you log raw request bodies? For PHI we want to ensure no raw text persisted.
05:18 Jonah: By default we persist minimal logs, but we can enable redaction and avoid storing request bodies for specific routes. We'll show config.
05:26 Samira: So recap — we propose a 6-month extension starting Feb 16, phase EU rollout in March with 4-node pool, APAC pilot in May, and a bench to validate p99 latency. Action items are Samira to send quote, Jonah to share technical docs, Priya to confirm compliance list.
05:45 Elena: That works. Timeline-wise we need the contract in hand by Dec 23 to sign before holiday freeze.
05:52 Samira: We'll aim for that. Jonah, can you kick off the bench prep?
05:55 Jonah: Yes I'll provision a mirror EU pool and send the bench plan and the spreadsheet.
06:00 Marcus: Quick note — please include cost per 1M tokens and expected infra ops overhead, that helps our finance.
06:06 Samira: Will do.
06:08 (short silence as notes are shared)
06:15 Priya: another quick operational question — for rolling upgrades how long is maintenance window on dedicated nodes?
06:20 Jonah: Typically we do rolling restarts and maintain capacity; expected per-node drain is 5-10 minutes and the autoscaler helps. For major kernel changes we schedule a 30m window but it's planned.
06:34 Elena: Alright do we have any blockers that prevent the extension?
06:39 Marcus: From ML perf side, we just need the bench to match p99. From Ops side, Priya needs the doc set. From legal we'll need redlines but shouldn't be a blocker.
06:49 Samira: Great. Anything else?
06:51 Elena: No, thanks all.
06:54 Samira: Thanks everyone we'll follow up with the quote and docs. Bye.
